metadataReview.note: Reviewed location: the 1972 siege centred on the town of An Lộc, capital of Bình Long Province. Indiana University Press describes Willbanks's study as the account of the 60-day siege of An Lộc in Bình Long province; the cited Wikipedia revision places the battle at An Lộc, provincial capital, 13 April–20 July 1972. The point is the GeoNames populated place Bình Long, which lists An Loc among its names. It is a town reference, not the perimeter, a troop position or the outlying Highway 13 fighting. The existing dates are retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: GeoNames record 1580349 (populated place Bình Long, population 15,000) publishes GeoCoordinates latitude 11.64711 and longitude 106.60586; its full-text search entry lists An Loc and Hớn Quản among the alternate names of the same place. Rounded to [106.6059,11.6471]. This is a town reference point for the besieged provincial capital, not a surveyed defensive perimeter, a unit position or the centre of the wider Bình Long fighting. The OSM quarter Khu phố An Lộc (relation 21109835), with the Bình Long market inside it, has its Nominatim centre about 0.7 km north-west of the point, and the OSM place=town node Bình Long is about 0.6 km away, both inside the old town. The present-day administrative ward polygon (OSM Phường An Lộc, centroid about 4.5 km north) is not used. No positional accuracy radius is claimed.
